results.statement: sc-lint must be a layered design.  w/ layers (lowest to highest):  a) sc-lint-types (shared types) and sc-lint-attribute (shared attributes)  b) independent cargo tools (i.e. sc-lint-boundary)  c) sc-lint cli which calls into (b)  d) just template (recommended just command layout w/ recommended mapping to (b) and (c) )
results.deterministic_check: cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps: sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime depend on no sc-lint-* crate outside sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support, sc-lint-attributes; those (a) crates depend on no (b) or (c) crate; docs/architecture.md has a Layered Architecture section naming layers (a)-(d)

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.
criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.

addressed.instructions: The layers of `anchor.statement`, by crate: (a) shared crates sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support, sc-lint-attributes; (b) independent analyzers sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability, sc-lint-runtime, which depend only on (a); (c) the sc-lint CLI crate, which calls into (b) and only forwards; (d) the adoption kit, bootstrap scripts and just template, which call (b) and (c). Does `item.text` keep its changes inside this layering: each change in a named layer, and every dependency it adds pointing from a higher layer to a lower one? Count it as yes when the item's changes fit the layering, even if the item does not restate the layering.

criteria.yes: Every change the item plans sits in one of the named layers, and any edit outside its main layer is stated as a compile requirement or a call from a higher layer into a lower one.
criteria.no: The item plans a change that does not fit any layer, adds a dependency between analyzers or from a lower layer to a higher one, or changes code without saying which layer it belongs to.
criteria.unclear: The item does not say enough about which crates or files it changes to tell.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something the layering in `anchor.statement` rules out? Violations, each one enough on its own: any of sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime gaining a dependency on another of those three crates (for example sc-lint-portability depending on sc-lint-boundary); any of sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime depending on the sc-lint CLI crate; sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support or sc-lint-attributes depending on an analyzer or on the CLI; analyzer rule logic (matching, filtering or deciding findings, for example PORT-006 prefix checks) placed in the CLI crate (crates/sc-lint, including dispatch.rs) or in a shared crate; the CLI interpreting analyzer configuration instead of forwarding it. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item plans at least one of the listed violations.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item plans a listed violation.
criteria.unclear: The item might plan a listed violation but the text is ambiguous.

addressed.instructions: What each issue asks: #193 first install never overwrites a consumer file (exit 2 with the paths); CI uses the vendored action ./plugins/sc-lint/.github/actions/setup-sc-lint; no action files when ci.enabled is false. #194 kit justfile has no set/default; install key justfile.windows_shell renders set windows-shell only if the consumer has none; install.py --dry-run runs just --list and exits 2 naming collisions; the kit skill's migration covers lint/test/default/set. #200 sc-lint lint <analyzer> exits nonzero on status fail; the bootstrap exports SC_LINT_BIN and puts the managed binary first on PATH. #201 each analyzer reads [tool.sc-lint.analyzers.<name>] with enabled, reason, exclude_rules, fail_rules, exclude_paths plus its own keys, unknown keys are errors; --rule-filter on every backend, forwarded by sc-lint lint; the kit renders and publishes the keys. #202 portability reads config_home_env and unix_path_prefixes (shared by PORT-001 and PORT-006) from [tool.sc-lint.analyzers.portability]. #203 boundary inventory: lib target name from cargo metadata, opaque [extensions.<namespace>] per record, allowed_dev_dependencies. #204 SCB-CYCLE-002/003: record the callee, exclude private-helper and receiver delegation unless in a multi-node cycle, exclude enum-variant expressions. Does `item.text` name the issue or issues it addresses (in its heading or per deliverable), and is every deliverable either something those issues ask for or something the change strictly needs (tests, the one doc that states the changed contract, a compile fix)? A test deliverable does not need its own issue number.

criteria.yes: The item names its issue(s), and every deliverable is required by them or strictly needed to implement them.
criteria.no: The item names no issue, or at least one deliverable does something none of the issues asks for and the change does not need.
criteria.unclear: The deliverables are too vague to compare with the issues.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` add work none of #193-#204 asks for? Examples: refactors or renames not needed by the change; new traits, registries or abstractions beyond what the change needs; a flag, option or configuration key the issue does not name (for example a --fail-on flag for #200, whose fix is a fixed nonzero exit code); process artifacts (gate matrices, ledgers, approval rows, certificates); documentation beyond the contract the change alters. A test, a compile-required edit, or a helper the issue's change directly calls is not extra work. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item plans at least one such addition.
criteria.no: The item plans no such addition.
criteria.unclear: The item might plan such an addition but the text is ambiguous.

relevant.instructions: Is the item a sprint bead: a unit of development work with numbered deliverables and a Design section describing code to write? A phase root or epic that lists sprints and decisions, with no code of its own to implement, is not a sprint bead.

criteria.no: The item is a phase root, epic or other non-sprint bead.

addressed.instructions: For each numbered deliverable in `item.text`, does the Design give the code or the exact edit: a fenced code block, an exact file/line replacement, or a signature followed by a `<redacted: N of M code lines are in the plan but were not sent to Jev>` marker? The redaction marker means the full code is in the plan and counts as code present. A one-line exact instruction (delete lines 1-4; replace X with Y in file F) counts as an exact edit.

criteria.yes: Every numbered deliverable has code, an exact edit, or a redacted code block in the Design.
criteria.no: At least one numbered deliverable has only prose with no code and no exact edit.
criteria.unclear: The deliverables and the Design cannot be matched up.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` leave a design decision to the developer? Signs: 'choose', 'decide', 'TBD', 'as appropriate', 'if needed', 'either ... or ...' about how to build something, or a deliverable described only by its goal. A redaction marker is not a missing decision. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item leaves at least one design decision to the developer.
criteria.no: The item leaves no design decision to the developer.
criteria.unclear: The text might leave a decision open but is ambiguous.
